headline: Debora fell at home on 2026-10-02 and has since lost independence with bathing and lower-body dressing, while her spouse and caregiver Kevin reports exhaustion and asks for respite.

items.statement: Debora fell in the kitchen on 2026-10-02 while reaching for a cabinet. Kevin found her on the floor. She denied head strike or loss of consciousness and had a small left forearm skin tear. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: The nursing note confirms every detail: the date, the kitchen, reaching for a cabinet, Kevin finding her, no head strike or loss of consciousness, the skin tear, high fall risk and the PT referral.

items.statement: PT evaluation on 2026-10-05 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommends a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, with PT twice weekly for strength and balance.
items.verifier_note: The PT note matches on gait, intermittent cane use, a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds, the walker, home safety evaluation, grab bars and PT twice weekly.

items.statement: OT reassessment on 2026-10-26 found Debora now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing; she was independent at the last review. OT recommends a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: The OT note matches on moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, independence at the last review, and the three recommendations.

items.statement: On 2026-10-19 the home care aide gave hands-on help getting Debora out of the tub. Debora said she has been skipping showers because she is afraid of slipping.
items.verifier_note: The home care aide note confirms hands-on help getting out of the tub and Debora skipping showers for fear of slipping.

items.statement: On 2026-10-13 Kevin, her spouse and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep and worry about managing evenings alone. He requested respite. The social worker discussed respite options and a caregiver support group.
items.verifier_note: The social work note matches on Kevin's exhaustion, poor sleep, worry about evenings alone, the respite request, and the discussion of respite options and a support group.

items.statement: Sertraline 25 MG was started on 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14), and the pharmacist updated the blister pack on 2026-09-15. The PCP planned a recheck in 4 weeks. No recheck or repeat PHQ-9 appears in the notes provided. The 2026-10-02 fall came after the start.
items.verifier_note: The sertraline start, the PHQ-9 of 14, the pharmacist's blister pack update, the 4-week recheck plan and the fall timing all match the sources. No recheck appears in the cited notes.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded for the current season, which began 2026-08-01. The last recorded dose was 2026-04-25.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows no flu vaccine this season (season start 2026-08-01) and a last dose on 2026-04-25.

questions_for_team: How and when will the PT, OT and home safety recommendations be put in place: walker, tub transfer bench, handheld shower, grab bars and added bathing hours?
What respite and evening support can be offered to Kevin, and how soon?
Has the 4-week sertraline follow-up and repeat PHQ-9 happened? Should mood be reassessed given her fear of showering and the recent fall?
Does the team want to review her medications as part of the fall work-up, given sertraline was started 2026-09-13 and she fell on 2026-10-02?
Who will offer the flu vaccine for this season?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) against the last IDT review and note any events between enrollment (2026-01-04) and window start that were not covered.
Falls and near-falls since last review: count, circumstances, injuries, and whether any fall occurred while on new sertraline or on metoprolol (dizziness, orthostasis).

ED visits and hospital admissions in the window, especially for cardiac symptoms (chest pain, ischemic heart disease follow-up), COPD exacerbation, or sinusitis; check discharge summaries for medication changes.

Medication reconciliation: sertraline 25 mg started 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14). Verify the start is documented with prescriber, check for follow-up PHQ-9 and any bleeding or GI symptoms given concurrent clopidogrel, and check for hyponatremia labs if ordered.

Medication reconciliation for other active drugs: confirm fluticasone/salmeterol and albuterol (both started 2026-04-25) are being used and inhaler technique/adherence is reviewed; confirm metoprolol, clopidogrel, simvastatin, nitroglycerin spray (check expiry), and levothyroxine are still active with no unexplained stops or dose changes.

Cardiac and vital sign trends in the window: blood pressure and resting heart rate (on metoprolol), any new chest pain or nitroglycerin use, and lipid/CBC monitoring due for clopidogrel and statin therapy.
Thyroid status: check whether TSH was drawn on schedule for idiopathic atrophic hypothyroidism on levothyroxine, and whether fatigue or weight change is noted.
Weight and BMI trend across the window (BMI 30+ with prediabetes): compare to prior values, and check glucose or HbA1c results and any diet or activity plan follow-up.

Respiratory and pain function: COPD symptom control, oxygen saturation, dyspnea scores, and chronic pain scores and analgesic use; check for opioid or NSAID use that could interact with clopidogrel or sertraline.

Mood, cognition, and social context: repeat PHQ-9 or equivalent, suicide-risk screen per protocol after new antidepressant start, cognitive screen if due, ADL/IADL changes, caregiver or social support changes, and attendance at PACE day services and transport. Also check care-plan items due (assessments, care plan review date, and breast cancer survivorship surveillance status) and list them for the IDT to discuss, without making treatment recommendations.
